items.description: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides over the next two days may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible 2 hours either side of high tide on Tuesday morning, Tuesday evening, and Wednesday morning. 
Areas particularly at risk include Torbay, Teignmouth, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish. Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths.  
The high tide at Teignmouth on Tuesday morning is at 9am, times of high water will vary along the coast.  The forecast total high tide level is 2.37mAOD, which is 0.22 metres above tide table level.  Strong force 5-6, south easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 1m are forecast over the high tide.
Similar coastal conditions are expected for Tuesday evening's high tide at 9:15pm, with a slightly higher tide level. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . 
This message will be updated by 3:00PM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.description: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
items.eaAreaName: Kent, South London and East Sussex

floodArea.county: Greater London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow, Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth

items.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 3:00 PM to 7:00 PM on 29/09/2026. 
The forecast high tide at Richmond is 4.63 mAOD at 5:00 PM on 29/09/2026.

We believe there is a possibility of flooding for Putney Embankment (SW15), Chiswick Mall and Strand on the Green (W4), Thames Bank at Mortlake (SW14), Ranelagh Drive (TW1), Friars Lane and Water Lane (TW9), Riverside and The Embankment at Twickenham, and the Towpath below Teddington Lock. Flooding of properties is not expected.

Astronomical tide levels are falling. The river flow at Teddington Weir is 4 cubic metres per second and is steady. We anticipate the flows to remain steady over the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . 
This message will be updated by 8:00PM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 06:30am to 10:30am on Tuesday 29th September 2026. 
Areas most at risk are around Hunstanton seafront. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 4.58mAODN at 08:30am on 29 September 2026, Wind Force 5, Easterly. The current series of high spring tides has now reached its peak and will fall away over the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded around high tide. 
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

floodArea.county: Gateshead, Newcastle upon Tyne, North Tyneside, South Tyneside

items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. 
The previous tide of concern has now passed,  the weather is more settled and no flooding is expected.   
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.   
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger. Never drive through flood water,  just 30cm of fast flowing water is enough to move your car.

items.description: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
items.message:
High tides this afternoon may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 1.15pm and 3:15pm today, Tuesday 29th September. 
Clacton Promenade, Lee-over-Sands and Brightlingsea sea front may see some wave overtopping and spray. The Strood at Mersea Island, Coast Road and car parks on the front at West Mersea, and the Hythe and Promenade at Maldon may be flooded. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at  Clacton of 2.73mAODN at 1:15pm, on Tuesday 29th September, which is 0.15m above tide tables, Wind Force 4, Easterly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 30 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

High tides on Tuesday may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible for 1 hour either side of Tuesday afternoon's tide at 13:30 on 29/09/2026. The weather increases tide table values by 0.49 m. Total forecast tide is 6.90 metres Chart Datum (3.63 mAOD) at Shoreham. Light South Easterly Force 4 wind. The tide will come close to the top of walls and slipways in Shoreham Town. Minor impact flooding will affect Sussex Yacht Club. Riverbank houseboats will be raised higher than normal, making access to them temporarily more difficult. Wednesday's tide at 01:45 30/09/2026 is forecast to be 5 cm lower (3.58 mAOD).  No further flood impacts are expected. We are closely monitoring the situation.  Consider activating any flood protection products you may have.  This message will be updated by 06:00 PM on 29/09/2026
